request.input_head:
Here are our documents.

=== Notes ===
Sample (fictional)

Breckwater Valley Robotics Club - Board Meeting Notes
Tuesday, November 3, 2026, 6:30 p.m., Mill Road shop

Present: Ruth Ellingboe (Board Chair), Glenn Asheford (Treasurer), Tomas Vrba (Program Coordinator), Priya Lindqvist (Coach), Dale Kucharski (Board Member)

1. Wickline Rural Futures Fund

Tomas reported that Hana Ostberg, program officer at the Wickline Rural Futures Fund, invited us to present on December 9. She asked for a short deck in advance. Ruth moved that we ask Wickline for $37,400 to fund the full FY2027 expansion for one year: second van ($9,800), third coach stipend ($12,000), kits for three new teams ($11,400), and added travel ($4,200). Glenn confirmed the figures match the FY2026 annual report and that the $148,600 base budget is covered by our five current sources. Motion carried 5-0.

Deadline: Tomas will send the final deck to Hana by Friday, December 4, 2026. Board review copy due to Ruth by November 24.

2. Instructions for the deck (agreed by the board)

- Keep it to eight slides or fewer. Hana said she reads decks on her phone.
- Lead with the 52 students who finished the season and the expansion to Ostrander, not the state championship placing.
- State the 14-of-18 postsecondary result with its caveat in plain words: self-reported, small group, no comparison group. Dale asked that we not imply the club caused it.
- Show the $37,400 as the four line items, and make clear Wickline money pay

response.draft:
Slide 1: Breckwater Valley Robotics Club
Proposal to the Wickline Rural Futures Fund
Presented December 9, 2026
Request: $37,400 for one year
Purpose: add Ostrander Rural High School and grow from 9 to 12 teams

Slide 2: FY2026: 52 Students Finished the Season
64 students enrolled; 52 completed the full season (81%)
Grades 9–12 from Breckwater, Ferris Township, and Calloway Consolidated
23 girls enrolled (36%), up from 14 the year before
41 of 64 qualified for free or reduced-price meals
38 of 64 paid no fee
Nearest engineering program: 140 miles away
Next: Ostrander Rural High School joins in FY2027

Slide 3: What Happened Inside the Program
End-of-season survey, answered by 49 of 52 completers:
44 felt more confident speaking in front of adults
40 used a club skill in a class or a job
In September, most students could not read a wiring diagram
By March, every team had 2+ students who could rebuild their drivetrain without help
1,180 optional shop hours logged, about 23 per completer
"I used to think engineering was something that happened in cities. Now I fix the pivot on my uncle's sprayer and I know why it broke." — Mireya, junior, Calloway Consolidated

Slide 4: What Our Seniors Did Next
14 of 18 seniors (78%) enrolled in college, technical school, or an apprenticeship
9 of the 14 chose engineering, welding, electrical, ag mechanics, or computer science
Limits of this number:
Self-reported by students and parents, not checked against records
Small group: a few changed plans would shift the percentage a lot
No comparison group: students who join may already be likely to go on
We do not claim the club caused this result
Starting this year, we are asking seniors for permission to verify enrollment with state records

Slide 5: What FY2026 Taught Us
The ride is the program: one van could not cover both routes; on late-van nights, attendance from those schools dropped about a third
More girls joined through a small Saturday build session led by Coach Priya Lindqvist
Demand is ahead of us: we turned away 21 students for lack of coaches and parts
7 of the 12 students who left went to harvest or calving jobs; we now call anyone who misses two weeks in a row

Slide 6: FY2027 Expansion Plan
Add a fourth school: Ostrander Rural High School
Grow from 9 to 12 teams
Serve about 85 students, up from 64
Needed: a second van, a third coach, and parts for three more teams

Slide 7: The Request: $37,400 for One Year
Second leased van, insurance, and fuel: $9,800
Third coach stipend: $12,000
Kits, parts, and tools for three new teams: $11,400
Added competition travel and entry fees: $4,200
Total: $37,400
Wickline funds pay only for the expansion, not existing operations
Our $148,600 base budget is covered by our five current funding sources

Slide 8: A Stable Base and a Plan for Year Two
FY2026 revenue: $150,400 from five sources; expenses: $148,600
No single funder provides more than 28% of the budget
Operating reserve: $14,200
After one year, expansion costs move into our base budget, supported by growing fee and donor revenue
Supported by volunteer drivers, a landlord who charges half rent, and families at our spring pancake breakfast
Thank you
Contact: Tomas Vrba, Program Coordinator
